sites.name: Intake 2 Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $34 per night Additional Vehicle Fee: $10 per vehicle per night
sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: Known for the fishing, Intake 2 is a small lake along the road to Lake Sabrina, just past the South Lake turn off. There are 5 walk in sites on the west shore of the lake and 11 sites suitable for small vehicles near the creek above Intake 2.
sites.directions: From Bishop go west on State Route 168 (Line Street) approximately 16 miles. The Intake Two Campground will be on your left.
sites.restrictions: Dogs must always be on leash and under owner control. Maximum stay 14 days. Active bear area. All food must be secured overnight and when not attended; bear boxes are provided and must be used (typical bear box size 48" x 30" x 36"). Always keep a clean camp and do not feed wildlife.
sites.reservations: No Reservations, Register at Campground Closes October 28, 2024

sites.name: Forks Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $34 per night Additional Vehicle Fee: $10 per vehicle per night
sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: Forks Campground is located near the junction of the South Fork and the Middle Fork of Bishop Creek. Most of the sites are tucked into the aspen and pine trees, some sites are along the banks of Bishop Creek. Bearproof food storage containers available in the campground. 21 campsites.
sites.directions: From Bishop, go west on State Route 168 (Line Street)approximately 15 miles. Turn left at the junction of the South Lake Road, the campground will be the first right turnabout 1/4 mile.

sites.name: Bishop Park Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $34 per night Additional Vehicle Fee: $10 per vehicle per night
sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: Bishop Park is one of the most popular campgrounds in the Bishop Creek Area. Located on the banks of the Middle Fork of Bishop Creek, Bishop Park has grassy lawns and campsites right on the creek. Many of the 21 campsites are walk in tent sites. Not recommended for large RVs, there are a few sites…
sites.directions: From Bishop go west on Hwy 168 (Line St) approximately 12 miles to the campground on the right.
sites.restrictions: Dogs must always be on leash and under owner control. Maximum stay 14 days. Active bear area. sites.reservations: Reservations Required. Reservations made using Recreation.gov. Closing Date: October 27, 2024

sites.name: Four Jeffrey Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $34 per night Additional Vehicle Fee: $10 per vehicle per night
sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: A large campground, 106 campsites, along the South Fork of Bishop Creek, this popular campground is usually open for fishing opener during the last weekend of April

sites.name: Big Trees Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $34 per night Additional Vehicle Fee: $10 per vehicle per night
sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: Named for the very large Jeffery pines that grace the site, Big Trees Campground is located along the banks of Bishop Creek and affords nice camping and fishing opportunities. Some sites in shade and some in open sunlight. Bear proof food storage containers available in the campground. 16 campsites.
sites.directions: From Bishop go west on State Route 168 (West Line St) for approximately 9 miles. The campground is on the left just past the 7,000 foot elevation sign.
sites.restrictions: Dogs must always be on leash and under owner control. Maximum stay 14 days. Active bear area. All food must be secured overnight and when not attended; bear boxes are provided and must be used (typical bear box size 48" x 30" x 36"). Always keep a clean camp and do not feed wildlife.
sites.reservations: No Reservations, register at campground. Closes October 15, 2024

sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.about: Walk down a short trail shaded by Aspen and Jeffrey pine to discover a stream side camp located next to Bishop Creek. This is a great base camp for fishing, hiking or just relaxing. This group site has room for up to 25 people and must be reserved. Walk in tent camping only. Campsite has a vault…

sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: Bitterbrush isa popular campground in spring and fall as it is frequently below the snow line or just has minor amounts of snow. 30 campsites. Bearproof food storage containers available in the campground.
sites.directions: From Bishop go west on State Route 168 (Line Street) approximately13 miles. The campground will be on your left (south) side of the road.
